prompt: In masked language modelling the loss is averaged over...
options: all positions of the sequence
only the selected (masked) positions
only positions replaced by the mask token
only the last position
explanation: Selected positions (mask, random or unchanged) carry labels; the others have none. Averaging over all positions divides by the wrong count.

prompt: In the 80/10/10 rule, what happens to the 10% of selected tokens that are left unchanged?
options: They are dropped from the loss
They are still predicted and contribute to the loss
They are replaced by padding
They become the separator token
explanation: They keep their identity in the input but remain targets, so the model cannot assume that an unmasked token is correct.

prompt: Of 2,000 tokens, about 15% are selected. How many are expected to be replaced by the mask token under the 80/10/10 rule?
For sentence classification into $K$ classes, a batch of $B$ sequences of length $T$ and hidden size $d$: which tensor does the head read and what does it output?
options: All token vectors $(B,T,d)$, outputs $(B,T,K)$
The `[CLS]` vector $(B,d)$, outputs $(B,K)$
The mean over the batch $(T,d)$, outputs $(T,K)$
The last token $(B,T)$, outputs $(B,K)$
explanation: Classification uses the `[CLS]` position, shape $(B,d)$, times $W\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times K}$. Tagging is the option with per-token outputs.

prompt: A classification head on hidden size $d=768$ with $K=3$ classes (weights and bias). How many parameters does it add?
In BERT-style extractive question answering, the answer is...
options: generated token by token by a decoder
a span of the passage chosen with start and end scores over positions
a class chosen from a fixed list
the `[CLS]` vector itself
explanation: Start and end scores of shape $(B,T)$ pick a passage span; the model quotes the document and invents no text.

prompt: In T5 span corruption, what does the decoder target look like?
options: The full original text
Each sentinel followed by the tokens it replaced, plus a closing sentinel
Only the masked tokens in random order
The corrupted input shifted by one
explanation: The target is shorter than the original text: sentinel, removed span, next sentinel, and so on.

prompt: A 10-token text has two spans of lengths 2 and 3 replaced by sentinels. How many tokens does the decoder target have (including the closing sentinel)?
Which statement about GPT versus BERT is correct?
options: GPT uses a bidirectional mask and BERT a causal mask
GPT uses a causal mask and trains on every position; BERT sees both sides and trains on the selected ~15%
Both are trained on the same masked objective
BERT is a decoder and GPT an encoder
explanation: GPT: next-token prediction with a causal mask, signal at every position. BERT: bidirectional, MLM at selected positions.
